topic: Blind replicated continuous-treatment ADRF over a fixed quantitative class. Observe finite-stratum X, bounded Y, and S_r=A+U_r; the centered independent nonidentical asymmetric errors have a uniform q>=8 moment radius and fixed near-origin characteristic-function lower modulus but may have open spectral zeros. Compact A support supplies the analytic source radius; latent densities f_x and outcome-weighted measures q_x have fixed H^beta radii with beta>3/2 and f_x is bounded below near the target interval. Prove analytic-cocycle identification of f_x, q_x, and mu(a)=sum_x P(X=x)q_x(a)/f_x(a), then construct a uniformly honest simultaneous band with width r_n=(log log n/log n)^(beta-1/2) and prove a matching all-honest-band expected-width converse. Use empirical-CF confidence-set inversion and constrained analytic sieves. Consumer: Melaku-Shi 2026 NHANES two-recall diet-mortality mvGPS. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Exact identities give F_x(s,t)=fhat_x(s+t)phi_1(s)phi_2(t) and G_x(s,t)=qhat_x(s+t)phi_1(s)phi_2(t); their ratios and cocycle recover the centered latent and outcome-weighted transforms near zero, with analyticity extending globally. At the EJS cutoff T_n of order log n/log log n, Fourier Cauchy-Schwarz yields the candidate sup-norm scale T_n^(1/2-beta), transferred through f_x>=kappa. The sinc^12 asymmetric witness, denominator, contamination, signed-measure, and prior-art checks all survived independently. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Establish the matching outcome-channel modulus by constructing contiguous Bernoulli-outcome alternatives with fixed positive f and compact-spectrum errors whose dose-response curves differ by cT_n^(1/2-beta), and match it with a uniformly honest band of width CT_n^(1/2-beta). EARLY KILL TEST: In one X cell with known smooth positive f, fixed sinc^12 errors, and Bernoulli mean 1/2+g(a), compute the singular-value modulus over an H^beta ball at degree log n/log log n; pivot if the H^beta-to-L-infinity separation differs from m^(1/2-beta) or outcomes permit a faster honest-band rate.

open_problems.open_problem: Is (log log n/log n)^(beta-1/2) a necessary expected-width order for every uniformly honest simultaneous ADRF band, even with one stratum, fixed smooth positive f, fixed compact-spectrum replicate errors, and Bernoulli outcomes?

source_refs.claim: Proves a compact-signal minimax density-estimation rate for blind repeated-measurement deconvolution using latent-signal alternatives, not outcome-channel alternatives.
source_refs.author: Jérémie Capitao-Miniconi, Elisabeth Gassiat, and Luc Lehéricy

source_refs.claim: Derives matching minimax sup-norm density-deconvolution bounds over Besov classes when the error distribution is known.
source_refs.author: Karim Lounici and Richard Nickl

source_refs.claim: Connects uniform coverage to lower bounds on expected confidence-set length through testing inequalities.
source_refs.author: Mark G. Low

source_refs.claim: Notes that sharp convergence rates for unrestricted Kotlarski estimators remain unknown and gives no expected-width converse for its confidence band.
source_refs.author: Kengo Kato, Yuya Sasaki, and Takuya Ura

source_refs.excerpt: This is the new admissible hard family: policy changes erase a hidden sign without changing hidden-depth occupancy.
The extra survival factor in this observed-law divergence is the load-bearing step.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing lower bounds perturb the latent density in a blind L2 problem or a density under a known operator; they do not show that the outcome channel remains equally ill-posed when the noisy-treatment marginal is fixed. The prior POMDP proposal supplies an analogous hard-family principle—hide a target-separating latent sign while controlling divergence in the observed experiment—but not the required Fourier construction. The first changed step is to replace its filtering recursion by a convolutional chi-square or KL bound for Bernoulli means 1/2+g_±, while keeping f and the error laws fixed, maintaining H^beta and probability constraints, and obtaining sup-norm separation of order T_n^(1/2-beta). Low's testing inequality must then be applied at a maximizing dose to lower-bound the supremum width of an arbitrary honest band.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A two-point or finite-packing theorem constructing admissible P_+ and P_- with bounded n-sample observed-law divergence and ADRF separation at least c(log log n/log n)^(beta-1/2), implying the same lower bound for the maximal expected width of every uniformly honest simultaneous band.

writing_exemplar.why: It presents sharp rates as an unresolved boundary of robust Kotlarski inference, naturally motivating an outcome-specific band-width converse.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Robust Kotlarski inversion gives honest latent-density inference -> its quantitative sharpness is unresolved -> an ADRF introduces a distinct outcome-weighted inverse channel -> an all-honest expected-width converse must prove that this channel forces logarithmic width.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its compact-support analytic perturbations and chi-square indistinguishability proof, relocating the perturbation from the latent density to a Bernoulli regression mean.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the blind-deconvolution degree asymptotics and indistinguishability mechanism needed to obtain the proposed logarithmic separation.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over localized Fourier or wavelet perturbations calibrated in sup norm and their testing reduction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its construction isolates the half-derivative H^beta-to-L-infinity separation that the Bernoulli outcome alternatives must retain.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the coverage-versus-testing inequality to convert contiguity of separated alternatives into expected-length and hence band-width lower bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A minimax risk bound alone does not establish a converse for every honest band; Low provides the required decision-theoretic bridge.

open_problems.open_problem: Can empirical-characteristic-function confidence-set inversion over constrained compact-support analytic sieves produce a uniformly honest simultaneous blind-replicate ADRF band with worst-case width of order (log log n/log n)^(beta-1/2) despite open spectral zeros?

source_refs.claim: Constructs uniformly size-controlled latent-density confidence bands by inverting Kotlarski moment restrictions without completeness, but leaves sharp rates unresolved.
source_refs.author: Kengo Kato, Yuya Sasaki, and Takuya Ura

source_refs.claim: Uses analytic approximation to obtain logarithmic minimax density rates for compactly supported signals with unrestricted unknown-noise spectra, but gives no simultaneous causal regression band.
source_refs.author: Jérémie Capitao-Miniconi, Elisabeth Gassiat, and Luc Lehéricy

source_refs.claim: Provides an asymptotically valid uniform band for a nonparametric errors-in-variables regression function, but its repeated-measurement route uses symmetric errors and conventional Fourier deconvolution.
source_refs.author: Kengo Kato and Yuya Sasaki

source_refs.claim: Derives Gaussian linearizations and subsampling bands for repeated-measurement density and distribution estimators, not an ADRF ratio under open spectral zeros.
source_refs.author: Daisuke Kurisu and Taisuke Otsu

open_problems.why_unsolved: The closest results do not compose automatically. Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehéricy obtain an analytic logarithmic cutoff and density risk but not an honest sup-norm band. Kato, Sasaki, and Ura obtain robust set inversion but only qualitative consistency and density inference, while Kato and Sasaki obtain regression bands through assumptions that avoid open zero sets. The missing proof step is uniform inversion of two coupled empirical-CF channels: the feasible set must control f_x and signed q_x jointly, propagate through q_x/f_x using the lower-density constraint, and retain stochastic slack no larger than the Sobolev truncation term T_n^(1/2-beta) through T_n of order log n/log log n.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit constrained-sieve band [L_n(a),U_n(a)] satisfying uniform simultaneous coverage at least 1-alpha-o(1) and worst-case expected sup-width at most C(log log n/log n)^(beta-1/2).

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation treats confidence-set inversion, rather than unstable plug-in division, as the robust response to weak or failed Fourier identification.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Repeated measurements yield Kotlarski restrictions -> plug-in inference is unstable near spectral failure -> observable complex moments can be inverted with uniform size control -> compact-support analyticity should make the resulting ADRF band shrink at a sharp rate.

method_exemplars.technique: Transfer its sieve-bias slackening, self-normalized maximum statistic, multiplier bootstrap, and Anderson-Rubin-style inversion to a joint f_x/q_x feasible set.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It already proves uniform size control without dividing by a potentially vanishing error characteristic function.

method_exemplars.technique: Use its analytic polynomial approximation, frequency cutoff, and compact-support risk balance to choose the sieve degree and bound continuation error.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its logarithmic cutoff supplies the candidate width scale after the H^beta-to-sup-norm conversion.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its studentized-process coupling and multiplier-bootstrap analysis for an errors-in-variables regression numerator and denominator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It has the same regression-ratio geometry and simultaneous-coverage target, while the proposed proof must replace ordinary Fourier inversion by an analytic confidence set.

open_problems.open_problem: Can the joint law of a bounded outcome and two noisy treatment replicates identify, within each finite covariate stratum, both f_x and the signed outcome-weighted measure q_x—and hence the ADRF—when centered replicate errors are independent, nonidentical, asymmetric, and may have open spectral zero sets?

source_refs.claim: Identifies a compactly supported latent distribution from two repeated measurements without restrictions on the unknown noise characteristic functions beyond coordinate independence.
source_refs.author: Jérémie Capitao-Miniconi, Elisabeth Gassiat, and Luc Lehéricy

source_refs.claim: Recasts Kotlarski identification as linear complex-valued moment restrictions that support inference without a completeness condition, but targets a latent density rather than an outcome-weighted measure.
source_refs.author: Kengo Kato, Yuya Sasaki, and Takuya Ura

source_refs.claim: Allows simple or isolated characteristic-function zeros, and arbitrary zeros under exponential-tail conditions, leaving the finite-moment open-zero-set regime outside its stated sufficient conditions.
source_refs.author: Kirill Evdokimov and Halbert White

source_refs.claim: Identifies and estimates a continuous-treatment ADRF by deconvolution, but its baseline theory treats the error characteristic function as known and only informally suggests estimation from replicated data.
source_refs.author: Wei Huang and Zheng Zhang
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B

open_problems.why_unsolved: The analytic blind-deconvolution result identifies a positive latent probability law, while the robust Kotlarski moments cover latent-density restrictions without completeness. Neither proves uniqueness for the signed measure q_x(da)=E[Y|A=a,X=x]f_x(a)da or shows that the same analytic cocycle jointly recovers f_x and q_x before division by f_x. The first proof step that changes is the analytic-contrast uniqueness argument: probability normalization and positivity cannot identify the outcome channel, so the proof must exploit shared error factors in the paired transforms F_x and G_x, establish uniqueness for a bounded signed measure, and only then form q_x/f_x.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A point-identification theorem giving observable local ratio and cocycle formulas for the transforms of f_x and q_x, global analytic continuation across open spectral zero sets, and the formula mu(a)=sum_x P(X=x)q_x(a)/f_x(a) wherever f_x is uniformly positive.

writing_exemplar.why: It directly motivates causal response curves with a continuously valued error-contaminated treatment and separates confounding adjustment from the measurement-error inverse problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Continuous doses define scientifically useful response curves -> treatment measurement error invalidates ordinary generalized-propensity procedures -> existing ADRF deconvolution assumes a known or conventionally estimable error law -> blind nonidentical replicates with spectral zeros require joint analytic identification of latent and outcome-weighted laws.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the analytic contrast and cocycle uniqueness proof for compactly supported signals, replacing one positive signal transform by coupled latent-density and signed outcome-weighted transforms with shared noise factors.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It solves the same blind two-replicate identification problem with unrestricted spectral zeros; the new theorem must extend injectivity to the signed outcome channel.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the conversion of Kotlarski derivatives into linear complex-valued restrictions, adding Y-weighted moments for q_x and cross-channel compatibility restrictions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its observable moments remain meaningful when characteristic functions vanish and therefore provide a natural formulation of the desired cocycle identities.

method_exemplars.technique: Use self-normalized empirical-CF inequalities, sieve-approximation slack, multiplier critical values, and Anderson-Rubin-style inversion.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After identification, these tools provide an inference rung that never divides by an estimated error characteristic function at its zeros.

open_problems.open_problem: Can blind analytic-cocycle deconvolution be embedded in a Neyman-orthogonal, doubly robust continuous-treatment score so that high-dimensional or continuous covariates can be learned while retaining a valid simultaneous ADRF band without a known error characteristic function?

source_refs.claim: Develops corrected-score g-formula, IPW, and doubly robust estimators under known Gaussian error covariance and identifies corrected efficient scores as future research.
source_refs.author: Brian D. Richardson, Bryan S. Blette, Peter B. Gilbert, and Michael G. Hudgens

source_refs.claim: Constructs a doubly robust pseudo-outcome for an error-free continuous treatment and proves kernel-based asymptotic normality with flexible nuisance estimation.
source_refs.author: Edward H. Kennedy, Zongming Ma, Matthew D. McHugh, and Dylan S. Small
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B

source_refs.claim: Discusses a doubly robust deconvolution ADRF estimator but leaves uniform bands and bias-corrected inference beyond its scope.
source_refs.author: Wei Huang and Zheng Zhang
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B

source_refs.claim: Provides robust empirical-CF inversion for blind repeated measurements but has no causal nuisance functions or orthogonality argument.
source_refs.author: Kengo Kato, Yuya Sasaki, and Takuya Ura

open_problems.why_unsolved: The donor methods solve separate obstacles: Kennedy et al. orthogonalize confounding adjustment for an observed dose, Richardson et al. correct causal scores under a known parametric error law, and Kato et al. invert blind replicate moments without dividing by weak error spectra. The missing first step is an observed-data orthogonal score whose pathwise derivative vanishes jointly with respect to causal nuisances and the blind deconvolution nuisance. Its proof must represent latent-density and outcome-regression perturbations through coupled analytic empirical-CF restrictions and control cross-fitted nuisance remainders inside a growing-frequency maximum process.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A stated orthogonal observed-data score and cross-fitted estimator with a product-rate remainder theorem, a uniform Gaussian or multiplier-bootstrap approximation over the dose interval, and an honest simultaneous ADRF band under high-dimensional nuisance learning.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames the practical co-occurrence of confounding and continuous-exposure measurement error and explicitly motivates an efficient-score extension.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Confounding and continuous-exposure error co-occur -> correcting only one source of bias is inadequate -> corrected scores provide protection under a known parametric error law -> efficient orthogonal scores combined with blind replicate inversion are needed for flexible ADRF inference.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the stochastic-intervention influence-function calculation, doubly robust pseudo-outcome, sample-splitting logic, and local-smoothing limit theory.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the canonical orthogonal representation of an error-free continuous-treatment curve; the new score must reproduce it using observable analytic replicate moments.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its conditional-unbiased corrected-score construction and M-estimation expansion, replacing Gaussian correction by a nonparametric replicated-error confidence set.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest causal-score treatment of continuous-exposure error and directly identifies efficient-score correction as the next methodological step.

method_exemplars.technique: Embed its linear complex-valued Kotlarski restrictions and weak-identification-robust inversion beneath the orthogonal causal score.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its observable construction remains valid at spectral zeros, where conventional deconvolution pseudo-outcomes are undefined.

literature_map:
Kotlarski (1967) supplies the foundational two-replicate factorization; Evdokimov and White (2012, Econometric Theory) relax nonvanishing to isolated zeros or exponential-tail regimes.
Delaigle, Hall, and Meister (2008, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:0804.0713) estimate densities and regressions from repeated measurements using identically distributed symmetric errors.
Comte and Kappus (2015, Journal of Multivariate Analysis, arXiv:1407.3495) remove symmetry for point estimation, not honest causal regression bands.
Meister and Neumann (2010, Statistica Sinica) treat oscillating error transforms with zeros and prove density/distribution minimax results, but not outcome-weighted ADRFs.
Kurisu and Otsu (2022, Econometric Theory; Journal of Multivariate Analysis) sharpen uniform Kotlarski rates and obtain density/CDF linearizations and subsampling bands.
Chen and Zhang (2025, Econometric Theory, doi:10.1017/S0266466624000379) further improve Kotlarski-estimator uniform rates within conventional density/error recovery.
Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehéricy (2025, EJS, arXiv:2409.02014) are the closest analytic anchor: unrestricted unknown-noise spectra, compact-signal identification, logarithmic cutoff, and minimax density rates.
Kato and Sasaki (2018, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:1608.02251) give unknown-error density bands using an auxiliary error sample or symmetric replicate reduction.
Kato and Sasaki (2019, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:1702.03377) extend multiplier bands to errors-in-variables regression without the blind asymmetric open-zero regime.
Kato, Sasaki, and Ura (2021, Quantitative Economics, doi:10.3982/QE1643) avoid completeness through complex moments and Anderson-Rubin inversion, but leave sharp rates unresolved and target a latent density.
Huang and Zhang (2023, JRSSB, arXiv:2211.04642) directly study a continuous-treatment ADRF, but baseline theory assumes a known error characteristic function and gives pointwise inference.
Kennedy, Ma, McHugh, and Small (2017, JRSSB, arXiv:1507.00747) provide the error-free doubly robust continuous-treatment pseudo-outcome; Colangelo and Lee (2023, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:2004.03036) provide high-dimensional DML inference.
Josey et al. (2023, JABES, arXiv:2109.15264) use replicate calibration or Bayesian imputation for causal exposure-response curves; Richardson et al. (2025, Biometrics, arXiv:2407.09443) use parametric corrected scores and call for efficient-score extensions.
Lounici and Nickl (2011, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1103.1489), Babii (2020, Econometric Theory, arXiv:1611.03015), Donoho (1994), and Low (1997) provide adjacent sup-norm, honest-set, modulus, and expected-width machinery.
The live intersection is coupled analytic recovery of f_x and q_x, quantitatively shrinking honest ADRF bands, and an outcome-channel all-honest-band lower bound under spectral zeros.
